title: SLO Sentinel — proactive limiters, routing policies, and anomaly detection for safe cost-tuning
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
This ticket implements 'SLO Sentinel' - a runtime-side service and control plane extensions that enforce latency and throughput SLOs during automated cost-tuning (batching/caching) rollouts. The goal is to allow the Optimize engine to suggest aggressive batching/caching configs and apply them safely by using proactive limiters, SLO-aware routing (traffic shaping by SLO risk), and anomaly detectors that trigger immediate rollback or throttled rollback when regressions appear.

Problem Statement:
Automated cost tuning (batching and caching) can reduce per-token costs but sometimes induces tail latency regressions or throughput instability under specific workload patterns. Past incidents showed silent regressions that only surfaced after customer impact. We need an automated guardrail system that: 1) quantifies SLO risk for a candidate config, 2) enforces runtime limits per-route/model during rollout, 3) routes traffic away from risky variants while collecting signals, and 4) detects anomalies quickly to revert safely.

Proposed Design (high level):
- Preflight risk scorer: static heuristics + lightweight historical-sample estimator that assigns a "risk score" to a candidate batching/caching config before apply. Scores: low/medium/high.
- Runtime SLO Sentinel daemon: a low-latency service colocated with the serving plane that can: 1) attach limiters (concurrency and token-rate) to specific model variants, 2) apply per-route routing weights (canary split, SLO-aware diversion), and 3) collect fine-grained telemetry (p95/p99 latency, queue times, drop rates, KB cache hit ratios, batch sizes).
- SLO-aware routing policy: when risk != low, the rollout policy will pin a maximum weight for the candidate (example: high risk -> max 5% traffic; medium -> max 20%) and route excess traffic to the safe baseline variant or lower-quantized fallback. Routing decisions take regional SLOs into account.
- Anomaly detection: streaming detector (EWMA + change-point + simple ML classifier) runs on short windows (30s/2m) and raises alerts when latency/throughput deviates from baseline beyond adaptive thresholds. Different detectors for cold-start, load-shift, and saturation patterns.
- Safe apply & rollback plan: 3-phase apply (dry-run -> constrained canary -> ramp) with automatic pause and rollback triggers. Rollback modes: immediate (fast revert) or degraded (throttle/remove batching) based on severity. All applies include an immutable audit entry and linked PR.

Implementation Plan (milestones):
1) Preflight risk scorer prototype (2w): small service that exports an API used by Optimize to label suggested configs. Unit tests and CLI for manual scoring.
2) Sentinel runtime hooks (3w): extend serving runtime to accept limiter and routing directives via control plane. Add lightweight enforcement of concurrency and token-rate limiters.
3) Telemetry + detectors (2w): instrument new metrics (queue_time_ms, batch_actual_size, kv_cache_hit_rate), wire to existing metrics pipeline, implement streaming EWMA detectors and simple classifier.
4) Rollout controller integration (2w): integrate with rollout engine to enforce weight caps, pause/ramp policies, and immutable audit logs.
5) End-to-end E2E tests & canary (1w): synth load tests with varied sequences, soak tests, and staged internal canary.

Observability & SLOs:
- Core SLOs monitored: p95_latency (target 200ms), p99_latency (target 800ms), throughput (tokens/s per GPU), error rate (<0.1%).
- Sentinel will create dedicated dashboards per model-variant showing split traffic, limiter stats, detector alerts, and a "safety score" timeline.
- Alerts: Pager for P0 regressions (p99 spike or throughput collapse), Slack + ticket for P1 detector triggers.

Rollout / Safety knobs:
- Default caps: high-risk configs max 5% traffic; medium-risk max 20%; low-risk allow 100% ramp subject to SLA.
- Rate-limited ramp: weight increases only after 10-minute golden windows without alerts.
- Manual override: SRE/PM can pause or force rollback with an auth'd action recorded in audit log.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Preflight risk scorer passes unit and integration tests and returns risk labels for >95% of suggestions within 200ms.
- Sentinel limiters enforce concurrency/token caps without adding >2ms median latency overhead.
- Detector false-positive rate < 3% on historical replayed traces and true-positive rate > 90% on simulated regressions.
- End-to-end canary: in controlled load tests, sentinel triggers rollback for injected regression scenarios and allows safe ramp for benign configs.

Open Questions / Trade-offs:
- How aggressive should default weight caps be for medium-risk configs to balance cost savings vs discovery speed? (Trade-off: customer ROI vs risk exposure.)
- Detector complexity: start simple (EWMA + change-point) vs invest in ML classifier requiring labels and maintenance. Initial plan favors the simple approach to ship fast.
- Storage of fine-grained telemetry: retention vs cost. Plan to store high-resolution for canary windows and roll up longer-term.
